```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(lme4)
library(ggplot2)
library(performance)

data("sleepstudy")
```

## 1. Introduction: Dataset Description

- **Dataset**: `sleepstudy` (from R package **lme4**)  
- **Source**: Belenky et al. (2003), *Journal of Sleep Research*  
- **Objective**:  Investigate the effect of sleep deprivation on reaction time.
- **Variables**:
  - **Reaction**: Average reaction time (ms) *(Outcome)*
  - **Days**: Days of sleep deprivation (0–9) *(Level 1 Predictor)*
  - **Subject**: Participant ID *(Level 2 grouping variable)*


## 2. Reporting Items Checklist (Overview)

I address the 6 key reporting items identified in last week assignment:

- **Software**: R package **lme4**
- **Sample Saizes**: Level 1 (*$N=180$*), Level 2 (*$N=18$*).
- **Estimation**: **REML** (Restricted Maximum Likelihood).
- **Centering**: `Days` is Uncentered (0 = baseline).
- **Model Specification**: Fixed/Random effects defined (See Slide 4).
- **Model Fit**: AIC & Deviance Test (See Slide 7).

## 3. Visualization (Spaghetti Plot)

```{r echo=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(sleepstudy, aes(x = Days + 1, y = Reaction, group = Subject, colour = Subject)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Spaghetti Plot of Reaction Time over Days",
       y = "Reaction Time (ms)", 
       x = "Days of Sleep Deprivation",
       color = "Subject ID") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 10, 1)) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "mako", begin = 0, end = 0.8)
```

## 4. Reporting Item 5: Model Specification
I specified two models to distinguish Fixed and Random effects:

- **Model 1: Random Intercept Model**
  - **Fixed**: Intercept, Days
  - **Random**: Intercept (per Subject)
- **Model 2: Random Slope Model**
  - **Fixed**: Intercept, Days
  - **Random**: Intercept + **Slope (Days)** (per Subject)

## 5. Result: Random Intercept Model
- **Input**
```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hide'}
model_intercept <- lmer(
  Reaction ~ 1 + Days + (1 | Subject), 
  data = sleepstudy)
summary(model_intercept)
```
- **Ourput**
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="75%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("result1.png")
```

## 6. Result: Random Slope Model
- **Input**
```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hide'}
model_slope <- lmer(
  Reaction ~ 1 + Days + (1 + Days | Subject), 
  data = sleepstudy)
summary(model_slope)
```
- **Output**
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="75%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("result2.png")
```

## 7. Reporting Item 6: Model Fit and Comparison
Comparison using Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT) and AIC:
```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hide'}
anova(model_intercept, model_slope, refit = FALSE)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="95%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("result3.png")
```

## 8. Conclusion
- Summary:
  - Sleep deprivation leads to slower reaction times (Fixed Effect).
  - The rate of decline varies significantly between individuals (Random Slope).
- Final Model: Random Slope Model is selected.
